newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle trade at standstill -feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle trade at standstill -feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets near midday on Tuesday remained at a standstill, feedlot sources said.
Packer bids were light at $64.00 to $65.00 per cwt and passed by owners pricing cattle at $67.00 to $68.00, they said.
"We're at pretty much of a stalemate, now," a Kansas source said.
Sales were not expected until Wednesday or Thursday because packers reportedly had comfortable supplies of live cattle after last week's active trade at $66.00, sources said.
Fed cattle prices this week were seen steady at $66.00, although a decline would not be surprising, they said.
"Prices last week went up too far, too fast, so I would not be surprised to see $65.00 by the end of this week," one source said.
Market-ready cattle prices could be pressured by fresh monthly supplies of formulated and contracted cattle available to packers as well as by hefty showlists, sources said.
Prices also could be weakened if beef prices trend lower following steep advances last week, they said.
